solves.reasoning: (A) Shannon was an American mathematician (not amateur). (B) interested in electrical devices (not obstacles). (C) part of the foundation (not conclusion) of AI. Choice 4 = mathematician-devices-foundation.
(A) famous for being the father (not unknown). (B) helped destroy (not preserve) German rockets. (C) became a full professor (not student). Choice 2 = famous-destroy-professor.
(A) was interested (not indifferent). (B) by inventing (not copying). (C) capable (not incapable) of learning. Choice 1 = interested-inventing-capable.
① famous: correct in context. ② capable: correct in context. ③ analog: should be 'digital' — his thesis was on DIGITAL computing theory. ④ biography: correct in context.
① electrical: correct. ② important: correct. ③ genius: correct. ④ protect: should be 'destroy' — he helped DESTROY German rockets, not protect them.
① ceased: should be 'continued' — he CONTINUED to teach for 20+ years, ceased means stopped. ② telegraph: correct. ③ engineering: correct. ④ foundation: correct.
'part of the _____ of Artificial Intelligence' — foundation fits as the base/groundwork. Telegraph, professor, biography don't fit this collocation.
'interested in electrical _____' — devices (장치) fits naturally. Rockets, thesis, biography don't collocate with 'electrical'.
'_____ to teach there for more than 20 years' — continued fits (continued to teach). Biography, scientist, telegraph are wrong parts of speech or meaning.
famous = well-known (유명한). obscure is antonym. notorious has negative connotation. ordinary means common/평범한.
connected = linked (연결된). separated is antonym. destroyed and invented are unrelated verbs.
capable = able (할 수 있는). unable is antonym. reluctant = unwilling. dependent = relying on others.
interested ↔ indifferent (무관심한). fascinated, curious, engaged are all synonyms meaning interested/engaged.
important ↔ trivial (사소한). significant, essential, remarkable are all synonyms of important.
(A) master's program = graduate degree (석사 학위). (B) tried to master = to become skilled/proficient. Choice 3 pairs (A)-graduate degree with (B)-to become skilled.
'an account of a person's life written by someone else' = biography. autobiography is self-written. thesis is academic paper. telegraph is a device.
'by _____ (invent)' — preposition 'by' requires gerund form: inventing.
'capable of _____ (learn)' — 'of' preposition requires gerund: learning.
'he worked to _____ by inventing a machine that helped destroy German rockets' — During WWII, he worked to help win the war. Other choices describe events from different time periods.

'part of the foundation of _____' — The learning machine was foundation of Artificial Intelligence. Not computing theory (that was the thesis), not engineering (his major), not information theory (he's the father of that).
